rite: He Greek Catholic. She Roman Catholic in 1873 to 1882. In 1857 her rite mark was first read here as Greek Catholic; the Demko agent reads it as Roman Catholic, and on a second look that is the likelier reading.
children: Mihály and János, twins, b. 29 May [1873], both marked with a cross
note: Whether the couple of 1857 is the couple of 1873 to 1882 is hypothesis H-022. No child is recorded here between 1857 and 1873. Names reused after a death: Mihály (1873, then 1882) and János (1873, then 1875). The four are kept as four people.

wife: Szlekár, given as Anna in 1874 and Mária in 1877, 1879 and 1883
note: House 120 in 1879 is next door to György Demkó at 121. One wife under two given names, or two wives, is not settled. Under ruling X-017 the change of the mother's given name between 1874 and 1877 is read as a possible second marriage, perhaps to a sister, until a record shows one wife.
Under ruling X-017 a change of mother between baptisms to one father is a second marriage until shown to be a second man: see H-031.

A second father named György Demko at Viszoka in the same years as FG-03, or the same man with an earlier wife. Under ruling X-017 a change of mother between baptisms to one father is a second marriage until shown to be a second man: see H-031.

May be the father of FG-03 or FG-04 with a later wife, or a third man. Under ruling X-017 a change of mother between baptisms to one father is a second marriage until shown to be a second man: see H-031.
A Demko daughter of the generation born about 1800 to 1812.

rite: He Greek Catholic, she Roman Catholic
note: No stated link to a Demko or a Duska. Why the owner kept the Kocsis entries is not known. Since B-009: Kocsis is the maiden name of Ahn 19 by the Demko agent's 1906 civil record (DM-D-008 @57861ad), which is why the owner kept Kocsis entries.

children: Maria, b. 15 Jul [label says 1868; probably the 1840s]

The earliest Krak in the folder.

husband: Mihály Bodnár; entered as Mihály Krak in [1846]
note: Landholding farmer. Godparents Pál Mraz and Erzsébet Hmily throughout. The husband took, or was given, his wife's surname in one entry, and his son János is 'Krak' in the 1870s with a later note that the correct name is Bodnár (FG-23, H-033). Two sons named János.
Nineteen years between the two baptisms, with the same godparents, Mihály Holubik and Zsuzsi Mraz, so one couple. Landholding farmer in 1845.
A Demko woman married into Senné by 1861.

children: Anna, b. 12 Jan [1871] (first begun as row 49 of 1870)
János and György, twins, b. 27 Jun 1877
note: One cottar couple over twenty-one years and seven house numbers. A Joannes Krak is godfather in 1875. The Michael of 1866 is a candidate for the 'Mihály Demko the younger' of FG-16. Two sons named János (1877 twin, 1885).

children: Mária, b. 11 Feb [1888], born illegitimate, legitimised 1889
note: Called 'the younger' in [1889]. The couple's first child was entered as illegitimate in February [1888] and legitimised in 1889, so they married between the two baptisms. Not the Mihály Demkó and Anna Batronszki of the Demko agent's 'maybe' strip, who are another couple in another village.

wife: Mari Csizmár in 1877; Mária Nyemcsik in [1896]
rite: He Greek Catholic. Csizmár Greek Catholic; Nyemcsik Roman Catholic
note: Not a Duska family: the surname is Danko. One man with two wives, or a father and son of the same name; nineteen years separate the entries.
Surname faint; more likely Danko than Demko or Dusko now that a Danko family is documented at Szenna.

wife: Anna Kováts [or Hováts]; her given name read as Mária [?] in 1875
rite: He Greek Catholic, she Roman Catholic
note: Two daughters named Anna two years apart: the first very probably died. Same godparents both times, Mihály Knyezső and Anna Ádám, born Hutkó. A candidate couple for the parents of Mária Kocsis, Ahn 19, born at Solymos about 1886 (Demko agent, DM-H-025).

rite: He Greek Catholic, she Roman Catholic
note: Mother's surname now clear: Knyezso, Roman Catholic. Their Mária of 1887 is the nearest fit in the archive for Mária Kocsis, mother of Maria Demko (H-038).

wife: Anna Cservenyák in [1843]; Mária Iv[a]ncsák [?] in [1846]
note: Anna Cservenyák is the mother before and after the entry of [1846]. So the B-011 reading of a first wife who died does not hold: either two men named Pál Kocsis lived at Solymos or the [1846] mother was misread.

children: Ioann, b. 6 Feb [1853] (mother read with doubt)
note: Cottar.

husband: János (Janko) Krak, properly Bodnár by a later note
rite: He Greek Catholic, she Roman Catholic
note: A later hand wrote beside the 1877 entry, in Slovak, that the father's correct name is Bodnár. He is taken to be a son of Mihály Bodnár and Anna Krak (FG-12), known by his mother's family name. He stands godfather to a Demko child in 1875.
No link to any other family in the archive is visible. The owner labelled the file with the mother's surname.

Kept apart from FG-25: different village, different godparents, and a surname that may be Danko.
Houseless cottar. She may be the Maria Demko baptised at Jesztreb in [1864] (FG-15).
A Duska of the Reformed church. Iňačovce had a Reformed congregation.

homes: Solymos; no house numbers in these years
note: The earliest Duska household in the archive. Two daughters named Susanna, eight years apart: the first is presumed to have died (rule 20). The mother's surname is written Plyuksa; a Pluchta family stands godparent to the next generation.
A second Duska couple of the same years as FG-34; János is not the János of 1834, who was seven in 1841. Two sons named János. Commoner in 1852, cottar in 1857.
One washed-out entry. A third Duska father of the 1840s.

Either András of FG-34 with a second wife, nine years after his last child by Borbála, or a younger András. A change of mother is a second marriage until a second man is shown (rule 20). House 44 is a Duska house again in 189[3].

wife: Anna Kitko (Kitzka; written Minda once and corrected)
note: The godparents János Hressan and his wife stand at every baptism. Two sons named György. The father may be the János of [1834] (FG-34) or either János of FG-35.

At house 33, where János Duska and Anna Hura lived in the 1850s. 'The younger' implies an older Mihály Duska alive in 1882. The Anna of [1871] may be the Reformed Anna Duska who is a mother at Solymos 43 in the Greek Catholic book in 1894.
The father may be the György of 1857 (FG-35), of [1852] (FG-37) or of 1847 (FG-36).
The father may be the Mihály of [1867] (FG-38). The child is one of two candidates in this folder for Michal Duska, Ahn 8 (H-041).

A family living away from the village, whose child was entered in the home book from a certificate. The father may be the György of 1876 or [1870] (FG-38) or of [1882] (FG-39). The child is the other candidate for Ahn 8 (H-040).

Also filed here, without being joined to the couple: Anna, b. 24 Feb [1898], daughter of Mihály Ku[...]s and a Zsuzsánna Duska; and János, b. 15 Apr [1920], illegitimate son of a Zsuzsanna Duska, who may be the Zsuzsanna of [1888] (FG-40). Three women of one name are possible.
The children are not Duskas; the owner's labels call them so. The husband's surname is written two ways.

note: The first Roman Catholic Duska household of Senné in the archive, and the first record that joins the Krak name to a Duska. Cottars. The son lived to 72: his death is noted beside his baptism.

rite: He Roman Catholic, she Greek Catholic
note: 'The younger' beside house 6 suggests a son or younger kinsman of Georgius Duska of FG-47, but a man with a child in 1879 was not born to a couple whose known children are of 1866 and 1868 unless they had earlier ones. The same godparents at both baptisms.

children: Anna, twin, b. 13 Jul 1907, d. 20 Sep 1909
Susanna, twin, b. 13 Jul 1907, d. 29 Oct 1918
note: A Roman Catholic farm servant, later cottar, of Senné, with children across the very years in which Michal Duska (Ahn 8) should have been born, and a gap between 1899 and 1907. Two sons named András and three daughters named Anna. The mother's surname changes from Minarcsin to Nyemecz: a second wife until one man with one wife is shown (rule 20); a third Anna in 1907 suggests the Anna of 1899 had died too. János Hornyák and János Hreha, both Greek Catholic, are godfathers throughout.
Either the György of FG-48 with a second wife and a new trade, or another man. A second household in which Michal could have been born.

rite: He Roman Catholic, she Greek Catholic
note: A Roman Catholic Duska living at Jesztreb, in the Senné book. Too old to be the András of [1868].

A Roman Catholic Duska woman married at Solymos, the Reformed Duskas' village.

children: János Kocsis and Anna Halász: Anna, b. 17 Dec 1891, d. 28 Jan 1894; Anna, b. 17 May 1906, d. 15 Apr 1908

note: Roman Catholic Kocsis families at Senné, next door to each other in the 1890s. The Kocsis of the Demko line are Greek Catholic, of Solymos. This Anna Halász is the wife of János Kocsis from 1891 to 1906, so the Anna Halász who is wife of the miller György Duska in 1895 (FG-50) is another woman or a misreading.
